title: What I learned shipping a local LLM in my first Steam game
author: whyduck64
selftext:
Hi, I’m Tarpo, a game developer with six years in the industry. I enjoy AI character chats and started making one for myself. That eventually became Idle Pixel Maids, my first Steam game: an idle maid café where you can talk to the characters. I put a local language model in it so players could chat without an API key or extra subscription.



Choosing the model took longer than I expected. A good benchmark score didn’t always translate into a natural conversation, especially across different languages and character personalities. I ended up trying the candidates through actual conversations. Of the models I tested, I liked Gemma.



Then I tried it on a friend’s gaming PC. It ran games well, but the initial model load still caused stuttering. Loading asynchronously didn’t make that work disappear, and postponing it until the first chat just meant waiting longer for a reply. That was an awkward fit for an idle game people expect to leave running in the background.



The experience has made me reconsider how I’d use an LLM in my next game. With chat, I had some room to work the wait into the presentation. I’d be much more hesitant to use that model for real-time NPC decisions, so I want to explore API-based approaches before bundling a whole local model again.



If you’ve put a local LLM in a game, I’d be interested to hear how you handled the first load.



Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5017140/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5017140/)

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body:
The point about benchmarks not predicting natural conversation is a useful one, and so is the load stutter on a machine that otherwise runs games fine. For idle games especially, "leave it running" is the whole contract.

If you go API-based next time, one thing that helped us is not making the model responsible for anything real-time. In Hatched, a browser city sim where every resident is an AI, a free local rules brain runs everyone by default, and the model is only asked about moments that matter, like a job offer or a fight. Players who want more can bring their own key (Anthropic, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible API), so there's no subscription on our side either. Did you consider a tiny model just for chat and plain rules for everything else?

https://hatchedapp.xyz
